correctness.rationale: For each active shift the prime Fourier uncertainty inequality gives \(p+1-k\) samples, and all support intersections sum to nine. Cauchy–Davenport and Vosper force all support pairs below \(6p-3\) onto common-step three-point progressions. The five explicit overlap-polynomial rows prove S=\(5p\)-e_- -e_+ -h. Vieta gives the exact minimizing and three-cancellation cases; five explicit coefficient pairs and one six-delay pair give sharp attainability. All hypotheses and boundaries (prime \(p>=7\), exactly three nonzero entries) are explicit. The embedded checker corroborates the symbolic law and finite geometry but is not used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The claimed novelty is the five exact low cross-STFT support levels, their gap to the sharp next level, the inverse progression theorem for all three-point support pairs, and a root-by-root coefficient classification. Krahmer–Pfander–Rashkov already prove the numerical minimum \(5p-4\): the candidate neither restates that as new nor attributes its supporting row-count argument to itself. Detailed comparisons to the full-text prior numerical bound, Nicola global extremizers and the available published self-window and two-sparse records did not find a theorem implying all of these claims. Historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: An unindexed specialist derivation could already contain the full low spectrum or coefficient classification.

value.rationale: The precisely motivated natural fixed-three-tap cross-STFT support problem has a complete low-support classification, a gap of length p-4 between \(5p\) and \(6p-3\), a sharp second-stratum onset, inverse geometry, and a complete coefficient test. It distinguishes cross transforms from self-ambiguity at the two previously missing levels. The published \(5p-4\) numerical lower bound is not presented as a new contribution, and no arbitrary parameter restriction or unjustified downstream significance is needed.
